(01:13:02): So yeah, so that's what Good Inside is. My co-founder and I are both psychologists. We've known each other forever, and we have a whole team where, yes, there's the podcast and Instagram. And I always consider those flags, like a strategy and a tip we hear, they're like flags. They're like things we try, but most of our struggle in parenting is we don't have a framework and an actual approach, which is the ground we would plant a flag into, which is why parenting feels like whack-a-mole where we're just trying things, right? Even though we would never do that at work. We don't even do that with gardening or tennis. (01:13:37): And so Good Inside and our app to me is the most modern, alive, personalized, technologically informed way of feeling like I have something in my pocket and someone and a community too in my pocket that can just close the gap between how I kind of want to show up and how I do show up. None of us close the gap completely, but I do believe we deserve access to tools that can help us do that. And that's what Good Inside as a business is built around.
turns.zh: 是的。正确的。还有本能，顺便问一下，什么是本能？这是我们迄今为止所学到的一切。养育子女的自然感受就是我们被养育的方式。这就是一切，一切都会很自然。所以我真的，就像我开始对我的社区感到非常生气，为什么没有更好的方法呢？顺便说一句，利用现代技术，这在您的手机上不是很容易吗？你不应该获得访问权限，不是为了让某个时刻变得完美，而是我们都会在艰难的时刻之后螺旋上升。这并不是螺旋式上升让我们度过了糟糕的一周。这是我们从谈论自己和不良模式的方式延伸螺旋的方式。过去几周。这些都是有利于我们和孩子心理健康的因素。我做到了，我开始生气，认为父母应该有一个更好的选择，让他们不羞耻地学习，不期望完美，口袋里有一些东西，将它与现代技术，现在的人工智能，这么多不同的东西结合起来，并保留人类的互动元素。 (01:13:02)：是的，这就是《Good Inside》。我和我的联合创始人都是心理学家。我们已经认识很久了，而且我们有一个完整的团队，是的，我们有播客和 Instagram。我总是将这些旗帜视为我们听到的策略和提示，它们就像旗帜。它们就像我们尝试过的事情，但我们在育儿过程中遇到的大部分困难是我们没有一个框架和一个实际的方法，这是我们插上一面旗帜的基础，这就是为什么育儿感觉就像打地鼠，而我们只是在尝试一些东西，对吗？尽管我们在工作中永远不会这样做。我们甚至不会在园艺或网球方面这样做。 (01:13:37)：所以 Good Inside 和我们的应用程序对我来说是最现代、最有活力、最个性化、最技术化的方式，让我感觉我的口袋里有东西，我的口袋里也有某人和一个社区，这可以缩小我想要的表现和我实际表现之间的差距。我们都没有完全缩小差距，但我确实相信我们应该获得可以帮助我们做到这一点的工具。这就是 Good Inside 作为一家企业的基础。

I think they're the most misunderstood kids in the world. They're labeled dramatic, oppositional. A lot of parents even tell me professionals tell them the issue is they don't punish them enough or they're not consistent. Those kids don't fear a loss of control. Their core fear is being too much and they can act that out and unfortunately get it confirmed by the world. And so my second children's book will be about deeply feeling kids and gives parents something. If our app is like the companion for the parent, I feel like the connection moment and for a kid to see themselves in this book is the purpose of that.
turns.zh: 所以是的，我的第二本儿童读物将于明年出版。所以我觉得这是我们第一次涉足实体产品。我的第二本儿童读物是关于感受深刻的孩子们的。这些孩子是我的热情项目“Good Inside”中的一个。我认为他们是世界上最容易被误解的孩子。他们被贴上戏剧性、对立的标签。很多家长甚至告诉我，专业人士告诉他们，问题是他们惩罚不够，或者他们不一致。这些孩子并不担心失去控制。他们的核心恐惧是太过分了，他们可以把这一点付诸行动，但不幸的是得到了世界的证实。所以我的第二本儿童读物将是关于深刻感受孩子的故事，并给父母一些东西。如果我们的应用程序就像父母的伴侣，我觉得联系时刻和让孩子在这本书中看到自己就是其目的。

turns.zh: 人们现在可以预订吗？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: It's called Leave Me Alone!: A Good Inside Story About Deeply Feeling Kids. And if you have one, these kids, the reason the title I think will resonate and honestly, a lot of people say, "Ooh, that gives me a lot of insight in my partner, someone at work." Is around their fear of being too much, they tend to have big explosive feelings and push the people away they care about the most in the exact moments they actually need them, thereby confirming their fears. See, I really am too much, which exacerbates the cycle until they know how to change it. So leave me alone is something a deeply feeling kid will often scream in their room when they're completely out of control and that's actually in some ways their deepest fear, not their wish. And so the title plays to that.
turns.zh: 这本书的名字叫《别打扰我！：一个关于情感丰富的孩子的好内幕故事》。如果你有一个，这些孩子，我认为这个标题会引起共鸣，老实说，很多人说，“哦，这让我对我的伴侣、工作中的人有了很多了解。”围绕着他们对太多的恐惧，他们往往会产生巨大的爆炸性情绪，并在他们真正需要他们的时候将他们最关心的人推开，从而证实他们的恐惧。你看，我真的太过分了，这加剧了这个循环，直到他们知道如何改变为止。因此，让我一个人静一静是一个感情深厚的孩子在完全失控时经常会在房间里尖叫的事情，这实际上在某种程度上是他们最深的恐惧，而不是他们的愿望。所以这个标题就是为了表达这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: How cool. Okay. We'll definitely link to that in the show notes.
turns.zh: 多酷啊。好的。我们肯定会在演出笔记中链接到该内容。

Before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that you wanted to share? Anything else that you want to double down on?
turns.zh: 您可以在您最喜欢的书商上查找。贝基博士，这有多有趣？多么独特的对话啊。我认为我们触及了人类各个层面的话题。在我们开始激动人心的闪电回合之前，您还有什么想分享的吗？还有什么你想加倍努力的吗？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Kind of I think before we started recording, I was saying how excited I am. I really mean it. You're like a major celebrity to me and my whole team knows it, that of all of the podcasts I've been on, they're like, "You must be nervous for Lenny." I was like, "I am." What I said to you is that I love your podcast because I just learn so much. Right. As a psychologist, CEO, obviously there's a lot for me to learn and I've learned so much from you and I really am addicted to learning. And the reason that's coming up for me now is I think about all the people who listen to your show who I think they're like that too. They're forever learners. They love to learn. It's why they love your podcast because you get so concrete and you follow the thread down the rabbit hole and it helps us feel more capable at work. (01:23:28): And one of the things I've found interesting is so many people who have that forever learner growth mindset, whatever you want to call it at work, we forget to access it with our kids. We say things like, "It is the way it is." I feel like people who listen to your podcast probably don't say that at work. That's why they're listening to their podcast. Maybe it doesn't have to be the way it is. Or, "Oh, I didn't know that before, but now I do. So I can try something new." And again, I'm never going to be perfect. Perfect is creepy, but I can grow. I'm more addicted to growing and learning than being right. And I think, I guess I would just ask anyone listening, especially as a parent, to say, "What if I just took that mentality home?" Like, okay, yelled at my kid. (01:24:06): I didn't mess them up forever. Do I know how to repair? By the way, did I have a parent who actually repaired with me? Because if I didn't, no wonder it feels awkward. I'm kind of the first person in my whole lineage to give a true apology to my three-year-old. Of course, that's going to feel hard. Or, yeah, I don't understand tantrums or I don't really understand why my good kid is lying to me, but maybe I could learn. I learn things at work all the time and I give myself credit. And what if I took that way of being and just applied it to this other area? I'd both, I think, be more compassionate with myself, but I probably also feel better over time about how I was showing up. And I just think we forget to apply that because again, parenting has been told as something that should just feel natural when it doesn't, right? So if we think of it as a set of skills, it's actually very hopeful. Oh, I learn skills from Lenny all the time. I can do that in parenting too.
turns.zh: 我想在我们开始录音之前，我就说过我有多兴奋。我是认真的。对我来说，你就像一个大名人，我的整个团队都知道这一点，在我参加过的所有播客中，他们都会说，“你一定为莱尼感到紧张。”我当时想，“我是。”我对你说的是，我喜欢你的播客，因为我学到了很多东西。正确的。作为一名心理学家、首席执行官，显然我有很多东西需要学习，我从你们那里学到了很多东西，而且我真的沉迷于学习。现在我想到的原因是我想到了所有听你节目的人，我认为他们也是这样的。他们是永远的学习者。他们热爱学习。这就是为什么他们喜欢你的播客，因为你讲得很具体，你沿着线索深入兔子洞，这让我们在工作中感觉更有能力。 (01:23:28)：我发现有趣的事情之一是，很多人都拥有永远学习的成长心态，无论你在工作中如何称呼它，我们却忘记了与我们的孩子一起接触它。我们会说“事情就是这样”。我觉得听你播客的人在工作中可能不会这么说。这就是他们收听播客的原因。或许事情不必一定是这样的。或者，“哦，我以前不知道，但现在我知道了。所以我可以尝试一些新的东西。”再说一遍，我永远不会完美。完美是令人毛骨悚然的，但我可以成长。我更沉迷于成长和学习，而不是正确。我想，我想我会问所有倾听的人，尤其是作为父母，说：“如果我把这种心态带回家怎么办？”就像，好吧，对我的孩子大喊大叫。 (01:24:06)：我并没有永远把它们搞乱。我知道如何修复吗？顺便问一下，我有一个真正和我一起修理的父母吗？因为如果我不这样做，难怪会感到尴尬。我是我们家族中第一个向我三岁的孩子真正道歉的人。当然，这会感觉很难。或者，是的，我不明白发脾气，或者我真的不明白为什么我的好孩子对我撒谎，但也许我可以学习。我一直在工作中学习东西，我相信自己。如果我采用这种存在方式并将其应用到其他领域会怎么样？我想，我会对自己更有同情心，但随着时间的推移，我可能也会对自己的表现感觉更好。我只是认为我们忘记应用这一点，因为再次，养育子女被告知应该感觉很自然，但事实并非如此，对吗？所以如果我们把它看作是一套技能，那它其实是非常有希望的。哦，我一直向莱尼学习技能。在育儿方面我也可以做到这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's such a beautiful message. What I feel is anytime I watch one of your clips and then do that thing and then it works, it's like, oh, that expands your mind. Oh wow, there's so much more I could learn. I should go deeper on what the hell I'm doing. I don't know what I'm doing. So that is a really important message of like you can learn this skill. It's not something anyone just knows how to do.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常美丽的信息。我的感觉是，每当我观看你的一个剪辑，然后做那件事，然后它起作用了，就像，哦，这扩展了你的思维。哇哦，我还能学到很多东西。我应该更深入地思考我到底在做什么。我不知道我在做什么。所以这是一个非常重要的信息，比如你可以学习这项技能。这不是任何人都知道如何去做的事情。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Yeah. And I like giving people very concrete things. So a question recently that I've asked my kids that have led to amazing moments just as a, is some version of, "If I could do one thing different this week to be a better parent to you, what would it be?" I guess it's kind of like a 360 degree-
turns.zh: 是的。我喜欢给人们提供非常具体的东西。所以最近我问我的孩子们一个让他们度过了美好时刻的问题，就像“如果我本周可以做一件不同的事情来成为你更好的父母，那会是什么？”我想这有点像360度——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. That's [inaudible 01:25:38].

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Review. Right. And-
turns.zh: 审查。正确的。和-

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Give me a raise.
turns.zh: 给我加薪。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Sometimes your kid says the hurtful things. "You can not be on your phone as much," which just get ready for it and just get ready to receive. "Okay. Thank you for telling me that." And I think the thing that stops us is we think our kid is going to say "stupid things." "You could let me watch TV." The truth is no matter what your kid says, it's a window into their world. And again, you can be the pilot who listens but doesn't open the cockpit door. "Oh, what would it be like to watch all the TV you want? Oh, your friends watch more. I'm so glad you told me that. Oh, does that mean I can watch TV? Sweetie, that's not going to be one of the things I budge on, but maybe here's something we could do instead." But just asking your kid that question and not expecting a profound answer. (01:26:16): It makes me think if anyone thought, "What if my manager asked me that question? Wouldn't I immediately just feel better about my manager anyway just from the asking of the question?" And I think it's just something so actionable that every time I do it with my kids, I notice their behavior's kind of better for the rest of the week just from that. And I want to give something high impact to anybody who's made it this far in the episode.
turns.zh: 有时你的孩子会说一些伤人的话。 “你不能那么频繁地使用手机”，只需做好准备并准备好接收即可。 “好吧。谢谢你告诉我这些。”我认为阻止我们的是我们认为我们的孩子会说“愚蠢的事情”。 “你可以让我看电视。”事实上，无论您的孩子说什么，这都是他们了解世界的一扇窗户。再说一次，你可以成为倾听但不打开驾驶舱门的飞行员。 “哦，看所有你想看的电视会是什么样子？哦，你的朋友看更多。我很高兴你告诉我这一点。哦，这是否意味着我可以看电视？亲爱的，这不会是我让步的事情之一，但也许我们可以做一些事情。”但只是问你的孩子这个问题，并不期待得到深刻的答案。 (01:26:16)：这让我思考，如果有人想，“如果我的经理问我这个问题怎么办？只要问了这个问题，我不会立即对我的经理感觉更好吗？”我认为这是非常可行的事情，每次我和孩子们一起做这件事时，我都会注意到他们的行为在本周剩下的时间里有所改善。我想给所有在这一集中做到这一点的人带来一些重大影响。

turns.en: I love that that's like the reverse of this approach to this episode is like from the work environment, what can you bring to your kids? And it's like, do a little 360, ask for what feedback can you give me in my performance review as a parent this week.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这就像这一集的相反方法就像在工作环境中一样，你能给你的孩子带来什么？就像，做一个 360 度大转变，询问你在本周作为家长的绩效评估中可以给我什么反馈。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 确切地。

turns.en: So good. Okay. With that, Dr. Becky, we reached our very exciting lightning round. I've got five questions for you. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 超好的。好的。贝基博士，就这样，我们进入了非常激动人心的闪电回合。我有五个问题要问你。你准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Here we go. What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
turns.zh: 开始了。您发现自己最向其他人推荐的两三本书是什么？

turns.en: I love The Power of Moments. I love Messy Middle and I got a lot from Creativity, Inc as well.

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a recent movie or TV show you have really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 最近有一部你非常喜欢的电影或电视节目吗？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: I really liked Secrets We Keep, which was actually recommended to me by our product leader on Netflix. And I really loved KPop Demon Hunters so much. I wrote a whole guide on it because I think it's just such an opener for really good, deep connected moments with our kids. And so those two come to mind.
turns.zh: 我真的很喜欢《我们保守的秘密》，这实际上是我们 Netflix 的产品负责人向我推荐的。我真的非常喜欢韩国流行音乐恶魔猎手。我写了一本关于它的完整指南，因为我认为它只是一个与我们的孩子真正美好、深入联系的时刻的开场白。所以我想到了这两个人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a product you recently discovered that you really like? Could be an app, could be clothing, could be a gadget.
turns.zh: 您最近发现有一款您真正喜欢的产品吗？可能是一个应用程序，可能是服装，可能是一个小工具。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: I started doing Liberty Puzzles. Do you know it? So some people-
turns.zh: 我开始做自由拼图。你知道吗？所以有些人——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 不。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Have heard of Stave. They're like these, but this is Liberty. They're thick wooden puzzles where they're kind of hand cut pieces. You never know what's an edge. Sometimes the colors that connect are kind of the end of one color and start of another, so they're tricky. But having this out at night, number one, I find puzzling is something where you have to monotask. You truly cannot multitask. And I find it so hard for me to monotask these days, even though it gives me such grounded energy. So that allows that. And it's something, yes, with my kids, but oddly enough, me and my husband will find ourselves doing it together at night versus being on the couch, doing work. And I feel like we're in the same world working on something together. And it's been really fun for that as well.
turns.zh: 听说过斯塔夫。他们就像这些，但这就是自由。它们是厚厚的木制拼图，是手工切割的碎片。你永远不知道什么是优势。有时，连接的颜色有点像一种颜色的结束和另一种颜色的开始，所以它们很棘手。但在晚上出去玩，第一，我发现令人困惑的是你必须单一任务。你确实无法同时处理多项任务。我发现这些天我很难单一任务，尽管它给了我如此扎实的能量。所以这就允许了。是的，这是和我的孩子们一起做的事情，但奇怪的是，我和我的丈夫会发现我们晚上一起做，而不是坐在沙发上工作。我觉得我们在同一个世界里一起做某件事。这也非常有趣。

turns.en: My kid has been really into puzzles recently. We have this menorah puzzle that we got and he's just every bedtime, he wants to do it four times, finishes it, again. He speaks Spanish because his grandma speaks Spanish to him, so he's like mas, una mas.
turns.zh: 我的孩子最近非常喜欢拼图。我们有这个烛台拼图，他每次睡觉前都想做四次，然后再完成一次。他说西班牙语是因为他的奶奶对他说西班牙语，所以他就像 mas, una mas。

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Oh, I love it. Love puzzles.
turns.zh: 哦，我喜欢它。喜欢拼图。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I love that he's just like, "Break it apart. Okay, let's start from the beginning."
turns.zh: 我喜欢他的态度，“把它分开。好吧，让我们从头开始。”

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 惊人的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. Puzzles. How fun. Okay. Two more questions. Do you have a favorite life motto that you find useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 是的。谜题。多有趣啊。好的。还有两个问题。您有最喜欢的人生格言吗？您认为这对工作或生活有用吗？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: This feels hard because it is hard, not because I'm doing something wrong. I just think this is so true in parenting at work. It's so interesting how often something is hard and we tell ourselves the story that we're stupid or we're not good at it. And there's something so simple about reminding myself, no, this feels hard because it is hard. I'm feeling this moment right. It's just hard. And I find that I always feel my feet on the ground again when I tell myself that.
turns.zh: 这感觉很难，因为它很难，而不是因为我做错了什么。我只是认为在工作中养育孩子也是如此。有趣的是，当事情变得困难时，我们常常告诉自己我们很愚蠢或者我们不擅长。提醒自己很简单，不，这感觉很难，因为它很难。我感觉这一刻是对的。这只是很难。我发现当我告诉自己这一点时，我总是感觉自己再次脚踏实地。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Great segue to our final question. So you're building a product, building a company. As a non-product person, what's something that surprised you about the experience of building a product and building a company?
turns.zh: 很好地继续我们的最后一个问题。所以你正在打造一个产品，打造一家公司。作为一个非产品人员，在构建产品和创建公司的经历中，有什么事情让你感到惊讶？

turns.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy
turns.en: It's funny. I'm hesitating only because I'm thinking of something and I'll say it, but I'm like, why did that surprise me? It should be so obvious. But I guess it's true that a company is just people. And before I started this company, I was in private practice, seeing people for therapy. And I feel like those skills are remarkably useful as the leader of a company where there's so many things I can't do. You're not going to ask me to financially model or data analytics, but I feel like there's really strong people who can do that. But I believe that understanding people or just having the skill of attempting to understand people is a surprisingly, but I guess also retrospectively obvious, really good leadership skill.
turns.zh: 很有趣。我犹豫只是因为我在想一件事，我会说出来，但我想，为什么这让我感到惊讶？应该是这么明显。但我想，公司就是人，这确实是事实。在我创办这家公司之前，我在私人诊所工作，为人们提供治疗。我觉得作为一家有很多事情我无能为力的公司的领导者，这些技能非常有用。你不会要求我进行财务建模或数据分析，但我觉得有真正强大的人可以做到这一点。但我相信，理解人或仅仅拥有尝试理解人的技能是令人惊讶的，但我想回顾起来也是显而易见的，非常好的领导技能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Dr. Becky, this was incredible. It's such an honor to have you on. I just see you everywhere all the time, have learned so much from you. And what a treat to have you in this podcast. turns.zh: 贝基博士，这太不可思议了。能邀请到你真是太荣幸了。我到处都能看到你，从你身上学到了很多东西。能有你来参加这个播客真是太好了。有人会问，“这里到底发生了什么？”我自己学到了很多东西，我知道人们也会学到很多东西。最后两个问题。人们可以在哪里找到您的《Good Inside》、您的书以及您想分享的其他内容？那么听众如何对你有用呢？

turns.en: Oh yeah, just goodinside.com. You can find our product there. You can find all the books that I've written there. You can find our yeah, newsletter if you're just curious to start there. turns.zh: 哦，是的，就是 goodinside.com。您可以在那里找到我们的产品。你可以在那里找到我写的所有书。如果您只是想从那里开始，您可以找到我们的时事通讯。所有这些都在 goodinside.com 上。我真的很喜欢反馈。因此，如果您在那里，如果您在想，“嘿，我在您的应用程序中，我希望您这样做。”我的意思是，你的听众是一个宝库，里面有出色的产品、营销，只是我自己永远无法拥有的想法。我们确实在努力打造一些东西，让父母总能松口气，感觉自己更有能力，并且父母拥有如何做到这一点的最佳信息。因此愿意分享反馈和想法。任何人都可以通过 DM 联系我，或者发送电子邮件至 office@goodinside.com，但这是一种提供帮助的方式。我喜欢向别人学习。
